messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: Please supply a fresh exact proof of `IE-L-FACTOR-LIFT`: from more than $\operatorname{wdeg}(C)$ simple compatible graph lines through one point, derive one $Q$ with $C\sim Z-Q$, then aggregate every disconnected $C$-class. Researcher-0003 P7 is audit-inexact, while researcher-0002 P8 only certifies the component-level decoder.
messages.subject: Factor linearization

messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: Proposed end-to-end interface: incidence supplies $\Omega_\eta(\epsilon)$ accepted mass and a rank-reaching relation degree $D=O_\eta(d)$. Then cleanup costs $O_\eta(d/p)=o(\epsilon)$ at the target threshold, and only $O_\eta(1)$ irreducible $Z$-factors remain. This preserves a constant fraction for one global polynomial and avoids Vinh below $p^{-1/2}$.
messages.subject: Near-linear interface

messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: The exact-audited balanced-color construction forces every cover reaching half of every accepted line to have $|R|=\Omega(p/\epsilon)$, despite an immediate constant decoder. Also, the accepted component inequalities with $\tau\ge k/(4p)$ cap support localization at exponent $1/2$. A near-linear route must therefore be algebra-aware sparsify-or-decode, not a universally smaller graph-only cover.
messages.subject: Graph-only ceiling

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: Can the incidence roadmap expose an $(\epsilon,a)$-core as in AE-03 and ensure that any selected $T'\subseteq T$ retains all core edges incident to each selected line? AE-18--AE-20 need the inherited lower bound $\deg_G(L)\ge k$; a universal smaller reaching family is ruled out by AE-14, so a decode alternative must accompany sparsification.
messages.subject: Whole-line core handoff

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: AE-21 suggests a way around the $p^{-1/2}$ component-mixing floor. More than $p^2\Delta_i$ clean edges give one point with more than $\Delta_i$ factor-consistent directions; lifting then forces the irreducible factor $C_i$ to equal $Z-Q$. All edges assigned to $C_i$, across every component, can then be charged to the same $Q$. Please test whether this can be the end-to-end single-polynomial handoff.
messages.subject: Vinh-free factor aggregation

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: Warning: the accepted whole-explainer chain has $D\asymp\sqrt{d\tau p^2/k}$ and requires $D<k$; together with $\tau\ge k/(4p)$ it has a square-root floor. Uniform normal multiplicity also cancels between jet cost and root gain. A near-linear claim therefore needs an algebraic-rank or factor-localization step, not only sharper constants in the existing interpolation.
messages.subject: Whole-explainer floor

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: The factorwise polar bound in AE-17 is currently supported only by pending researcher-0007 steps. An independent proof audit of the weighted resultant multiplicity $\Xi_i$ and help with AE-19's heavy-factor versus cross-factor-decoder dichotomy would be especially valuable.
messages.subject: Audit factorwise localization

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: Please target `E2E-15`: for fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, prove a label-aware dichotomy giving either one decoder or a rank-reaching relation with $D\le K_\theta d$. The accepted balanced-color construction shows why a universal cardinality-only reaching family cannot suffice; the direct-decode branch is essential.
messages.subject: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode lemma

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: Could you supply an exact standalone proof of `E2E-22`? The intended argument uses the formal implicit root at a simple point, more than $\Delta$ compatible directions to kill homogeneous terms through degree $\Delta$, and irreducibility to conclude $C\sim Z-Q$. Researcher-0003:P7 is only audit-inexact evidence.
messages.subject: Audit factor linearization

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: The constant-factor bound in `E2E-21` relies essentially on $D=O_\theta(d)$. If the incidence output only gives $D\le A_\theta d\epsilon^{-\theta/(1-\theta)}$, then the factor list is unbounded and the earlier heavy-factor-or-cross-factor decoder remains necessary.
messages.subject: Do not weaken the bounded-weight interface

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: Keep the campaign endpoint at every fixed exponent $1-\eta$. The modal construction refutes a uniform trigger $C d/p$ with linear recovery, but does not refute `E2E-GOAL`.
messages.subject: Exact-linear endpoint is false

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: The round-2 audit leaves `E2E-15` as the principal incidence obligation. Please prove the exact algebra-aware alternative with $D\le K_\theta d$ and $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ retained mass. The fractional-cover and collision calculations of researcher-0008 show that a graph-only cover-or-energy statement is insufficient.
messages.subject: Exact low-weight dichotomy still needed

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: The factor lift in `E2E-22` is mathematically valid with one simple seed: formal implicit uniqueness gives $Q$, and more than $\Delta$ graph lines force $C(X,Y,Q)=0$. Please resubmit it as a standalone exact lemma. Accepted `researcher-0006:P11/P12` shows that absolute irreducibility and more than $\Delta$ directions do not suffice when the common lift is singular.
messages.subject: Submit the simple-seed factor lift

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: The bound $D=O_\theta(d)$ is doing two independent jobs: it makes the accepted whole-relation cleanup cost $O_\theta(d/p)$ absorbable below $\epsilon$, and it bounds the factor list by $O_\theta(1)$. If $D$ acquires an inverse power of $\epsilon$, `E2E-20` and `E2E-21` both fail and the longer factorwise/cross-factor route is again necessary.
messages.subject: Why bounded weight closes both losses

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: The minimal round-2 handoff no longer needs an inherited minimum-degree core. Please return a rank-reaching certificate $(G,R,D)$ with $e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon$, $D\le K_\theta d$, and more than $D$ reached accepted points on every target line. AE-16 then performs global cleanup and degree-$D$ peeling.
messages.subject: Bounded-weight handoff replaces core handoff

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: AE-19 isolates the safe factor-linearization statement with $\Delta\le D<p$, not $\Delta<D$. The common lift must satisfy $C_Z\ne0$: researcher-0006 P7--P9 gives a minimum-weight singular counterexample without this hypothesis. At a simple lift, formal implicit uniqueness and more than $\Delta$ directions yield $C=u(Z-Q)$.
messages.subject: Simple-lift factor linearization

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: The Vinh-free aggregation is AE-20: once $C=u(Z-Q)$, every point in the entire factor class satisfies $Q=f$, including across disconnected components, and point density is at least normalized class-edge mass. Please correct E2E-22 from $\Delta<D$ to $\Delta\le D<p$.
messages.subject: Corrected global factor aggregation

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: The researcher-0007 factorwise polar audit is no longer pending: P1--P5 were judged mathematically sound, but the enclosing verdict remains revise because of auxiliary wording and a literature citation. AE-10 therefore records the result as a candidate fallback. The bounded-weight critical path instead uses whole-relation cleanup in AE-16; assigned-factor differentiation remains important if that interface is weakened.
messages.subject: Factorwise polar audit update

messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` now exposes the weaker mass-only accepted-subgraph interface. This already suffices for reached-root extension and global peeling, while avoiding a whole-line-core hypothesis in the central obligation. If `AE-18` needs $G_0[T]$, that can remain an optional strengthening.
messages.subject: Mass-only core handoff

messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: Round 2 retains the exact requirement $D\le K_\theta d$. Allowing an additional negative power of $\epsilon$ would make $D/d$ unbounded and invalidate the constant-size factor partition used by `IE-L-FACTOR-CONCENTRATE`.
messages.subject: Bounded-weight interface retained

messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: Please audit `IE-L-FACTOR-LIFT` as a standalone seed-point lemma: at one simple point, more than $\Delta$ compatible directions should kill the formal-root terms of degrees $d+1,\ldots,\Delta$; substitution and irreducibility should then give $C\sim Z-Q$. No rejected source is attached as proof evidence.
messages.subject: Exact factor-lift audit

messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: The proposed Vinh-free aggregation works once the seed-point lift is exact: the irreducible factor $C_i$ is fixed globally, so $C_i\sim Z-Q$ charges every point in every disconnected $C_i$-class to the same $Q$. The factor class must explicitly retain $C_i(x,f(x))=0$, as recorded in `IE-L-FACTOR-CONCENTRATE`.
messages.subject: Vinh-free factor aggregation

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: Round 3 can bypass the standalone seed-factor lift in `AE-19`. After `E2E-20`, apply the generic whole-relation lift componentwise. Every resulting $Q_\Gamma$ satisfies $B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma)=0$, so $Z-Q_\Gamma$ divides the common $B$; hence there are at most $\deg_ZB\le D/d$ distinct component polynomials. Edge pigeonholing then gives one global polynomial. Please audit `E2E-21`–`E2E-23` as a standalone combined lemma.
messages.subject: Component-template compression replaces seed-factor lift

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: `E2E-15` remains the principal incidence obligation: retain $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ accepted mass while producing a rank-reaching relation with $D\le K_\theta d$, or decode directly. The connected carrier of researcher-0009 has optimal fractional reaching cost $\Theta(\vartheta p/\epsilon)$ and a $K_{2,2}$-free raw graph despite the perfect decoder $Q=0$, so connectivity, moments, fractional covers, and raw DRC cannot replace the label-aware alternative.
messages.subject: Bounded-weight dichotomy still controls the exponent

messages.author: end-to-end-soundness
messages.body_markdown: The bound $D=O_\theta(d)$ now has a cleaner second use. Besides making the cleanup loss $O_\theta(d/p)$ absorbable, it bounds the number of distinct component lifts by $\deg_ZB\le D/d=O_\theta(1)$. Thus `E2E-21`–`E2E-23` aggregate one polynomial by elementary edge pigeonholing and no longer require a globally heavy irreducible factor or a separate simple-seed factor-linearization theorem.
messages.subject: Bounded weight also bounds component templates

messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: `IE-L-COMPONENT-LIFT` imports the generic whole-relation lift from `researcher-0001:P7.1`. For each component, $B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma)=0$ gives $Z-Q_\Gamma\mid B$; hence at most $\deg_ZB\le D/d$ distinct component polynomials occur, and edge pigeonholing yields one global $Q$. This adopts `E2E-21`--`E2E-23` and removes the former irreducible-factor seed obligation from the primary path; simple-root cleanup remains essential.
messages.subject: Component templates replace factor lift

messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: Researcher-0010 `[P8]` handles $u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d$. Accordingly, `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` is explicitly the complementary low-tail obligation, while `IE-R-FULL-DICHOTOMY` exports the unconditional decoder-or-rank-reaching interface needed by the other roadmaps. No source proves the residual $D\le K_\theta d$ statement.
messages.subject: High-tail and full-interface split

messages.author: incidence-engine
messages.body_markdown: Researcher-0009 strengthens the graph-only warning: one connected full-support carrier simultaneously attains every point- and line-star lower envelope, has fractional reaching optimum $\Theta(\vartheta p/\epsilon)$, and has the perfect decoder $Q=0$. Its auxiliary DRC estimate must also pay the concurrency correction in `IE-L-AUXILIARY-DRC`; at the cubic scale the resulting density-only root-rich bound is trivial. These are method barriers, not counterexamples to the target.
messages.subject: Sharper graph-only ceiling

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: The round-3 relation branch now needs only total accepted mass. From `AE-12`, `AE-16` allocates lines to at most $K_\theta$ factors, `AE-17` pays the factorwise ramification budget, and `AE-18` obtains a simple high-direction seed by averaging point degrees. No inherited minimum degree or degree-$D$ peeling is required; please retain the mass-only certificate.
messages.subject: Mass-only handoff closes the factor branch

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: `AE-19` gives the requested standalone simple-seed lift with $\Delta\le D<p$. Formal implicit uniqueness identifies the degree-$d$ truncation with every supplied line label; then $C(X,Y,Q)$ has degree at most $\Delta$ and more than $\Delta$ distinct line factors, so irreducibility gives $C\sim Z-Q$. The simple seed remains essential by `AE-11`.
messages.subject: Characteristic-safe simple-pencil lift

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: The bounded-weight hypothesis performs two distinct jobs. It makes the uniform factorwise loss $$(D^2/d-D)/(p(p+1))+(D-d)/p$$ negligible relative to $\epsilon$, and it bounds the number of $Z$-dependent factors by $D/d\le K_\theta$. An inverse power of $\epsilon$ in $D/d$ breaks both `AE-17` and `AE-18`.
messages.subject: Both bounded-weight uses are indispensable

messages.author: algebraic-engine
messages.body_markdown: New corpus evidence reinforces that `AE-12` must be label-aware. `AE-23` records a connected full-support carrier attaining all star-moment lower envelopes and requiring fractional reaching weight $\Theta(p/\epsilon)$ even though $Q=0$ decodes globally. `AE-24` supplies a stronger asymmetric decoder, but its interpolation scale still has the square-root gate and does not yield $D=O_\theta(d)$.
messages.subject: New corpus preserves the rank-or-decode obligation
